headline: LME copper drops 1.4% to about $13,600 as rate-hike bets grow
detail: Three-month copper fell to about $13,605/t Thursday as hawkish Fed talk lifted the dollar and longs sold out; COMEX closed near $6.18/lb. Lower copper futures usually mean yards trim #1 and #2 copper bids within days.

headline: Dollar hits a 19-month high as markets bet on a December Fed hike
detail: CME FedWatch showed about 89% odds of a quarter-point hike in December, and the 10-year Treasury yield sat near 5%. A strong dollar is the main weight on copper, aluminum and gold right now.

headline: Chicago November ferrous scrap settled higher: shred up $30, busheling up $20
detail: Mills paid $20-30/gt more for November scrap, with Chicago shredded up $30/gt and busheling up $20/gt. Firm mill demand and slow inbound flows are holding Midwest scrap up going into winter.

headline: Gold tumbles about 3% to near $3,866 and silver slips under $50
detail: Gold fell 3.05% and silver 3.47% Thursday as the dollar jumped and hike odds rose. The GLD gold fund closed at its lowest in 12 months.

headline: LME aluminum cash premium hits its steepest since 1990 as stocks keep shrinking
detail: Cash aluminum traded about $177/t over three-month, the widest backwardation in 36 years, with LME stocks down to 226,350 t, less than half of January. Even so, cash fell about 2% Thursday with the strong dollar.

headline: SMU's ferrous scrap price index rises across grades for November
detail: Steel Market Update said prices rose for all the grades it tracks, with gains varying by region. Higher mill buying prices support what yards can pay for shred, busheling and HMS.

headline: Steel sheet lead times stretch into 2027, some buyers see nothing until late February
detail: Average lead times now run into late January, and only about 5% of buyers say mills will negotiate on new orders. Busy mills keep buying prime and shredded scrap hard.

headline: Nucor raises hot-rolled coil price $15 to $1,295/st, the 17th straight weekly increase
detail: Spot US hot-rolled is trading about $1,340-1,400/st versus $825-865 a year ago. Strong sheet prices keep electric-arc mills hungry for scrap.

headline: US Steel and the Steelworkers resume contract talks today
detail: Talks restart Nov 13 and the union predicts progress; Cleveland-Cliffs already reached its four-year deal. A strike threat at US Steel would be a wildcard for flat-rolled supply and mill scrap buying.

headline: Palladium gives back its rally, falling about 5% to near $992
detail: Palladium closed around $991.50 Thursday after jumping to about $1,087 earlier in the week, and platinum slipped about 1% to $1,520. Lower PGM prices mean lower catalytic converter values this morning.

headline: Thailand tightens imports of copper, aluminum and steel scrap
detail: Thailand is drafting stricter impurity and importer rules and has stepped up customs checks, pushing some cargoes to Malaysia and India. Fewer Asian outlets could pressure US nonferrous scrap export prices.

headline: China's copper import premiums sit at record highs
detail: Shanghai import premiums passed $200/t as metal is pulled to the US and Chinese stocks shrink. SMM expects them to stay high through December, which cushions copper against the strong dollar.

headline: Turkish mill Habas halts steel output after a deadly explosion
detail: Production at Habas's Aliaga plant is suspended. Turkey is the biggest buyer of US export scrap, so a big mill down can soften demand for HMS cargoes.

headline: Strike at Teck's Highland Valley copper mine nears three weeks
detail: More than 1,200 Steelworkers have been out since Oct 24 at the British Columbia mine. It adds to an already tight copper concentrate market.

headline: Kazakhstan bans scrap exports for six months
detail: The ban, in force since Nov 1, covers ferrous, nonferrous and stainless scrap to keep material for local mills. It trims supply in world scrap trade.

headline: Mexico says its crackdown on Asian steel is working as US tariff talks advance
detail: Mexico cancelled about 1,100 import registrations, cutting some Vietnamese steel imports by up to 80% and third-country steel and aluminum imports by about 30%. Less transshipped steel supports North American mill prices.

headline: Canada serves Stellantis a default notice over its Brampton plant
detail: Ottawa says Stellantis broke a funding deal to retool the Brampton plant after selling it, as Jeep work shifts to the US, and gave it 30 days. More US assembly means more steel demand and plant scrap south of the border.

headline: New-car prices hit a record $51,109 as dealer inventory climbs to 3.1 million
detail: Inventory rose by about 100,000 units while prices stayed high. Fuller lots point to softer production ahead, which means less prompt industrial scrap from auto plants.

headline: Ford's October US sales slip 0.8%
detail: F-Series pickups and big SUVs gained while overall Ford sales dipped slightly. Flat sales keep auto steel and aluminum demand steady but not growing.

headline: 30-year mortgage rate eases to 7.11%, its fourth weekly drop
detail: Freddie Mac's survey fell from 7.18%, but it was taken before this week's hot inflation data pushed daily rates back up. Rates above 7% keep homebuilding, and its wire, pipe and rebar demand, subdued.

headline: Nonresidential construction forecast to grow only about 2% in 2027
detail: Data centers and power projects keep growing while chip plants, warehouses and public work fall. That is mixed for rebar, structural steel and copper wire demand.

headline: China's October steel exports fall 6% from September
detail: China shipped 9.85 Mt of steel in October, and January-October exports are down 2.3%; October iron ore imports fell 5.1% from a year ago. Less cheap Chinese steel abroad supports steel prices elsewhere.

headline: China's central bank promises more support for the economy
detail: The PBoC said it will keep policy loose with more lending for consumer demand and infrastructure. Stimulus hopes help base metal demand; October activity data is due Sunday night.

headline: China's big mills cut daily steel output 7% in late October
detail: CISA members averaged 1.76 Mt a day for Oct 21-31 and said demand remains slack. Lower Chinese output weighs on iron ore, which slipped to about $91.60.

headline: Importers press for $166 billion in refunds of struck-down tariffs
detail: A class of importers asked the trade court to order refunds of the IEEPA tariffs, with the Justice Department's answer due today. Section 232 steel, aluminum and copper tariffs are not affected.

headline: US and China extend their trade truce two more months, to January 10
detail: China kept its pause on some critical-mineral export controls and its 24% tariff on US goods, and the US extended 178 tariff exclusions. That avoids a near-term escalation that could rattle metals.

headline: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee calls October inflation borderline disturbing
detail: Goolsbee would not rule out a half-point hike in December. A more hawkish Fed lifts the dollar, which weighs on copper, aluminum and gold.

headline: Sibanye-Stillwater cuts US PGM output forecast after Montana strike
detail: Sibanye lowered 2026 Montana output to 245,000-255,000 oz from 280,000-300,000 oz. Less US-mined palladium and platinum gives PGM prices some support.

headline: Standard Chartered still sees gold at $4,650 this quarter
detail: The bank expects one December hike then a pause and points to strong ETF and central bank buying. Gold is now well below its $4,000 support level.
